strategy_title: Swap 2D Tile Fast Dim to Coalesce Transpose Loads and Stores
strategy_description: When a 2D Triton kernel performs a non-contiguous-to-contiguous transpose, the warp-lane fast dimension (the innermost arange axis) must align with the stride-1 dimension of each memory operation independently. If the fast dim is stride-1 for stores but stride-N (N>>1) for loads, every warp load touches N separate cache lines, causing 0% L1 hit rate, L2 saturation, and high L1TEX stall cycles. The fix is to swap the arange orientation: make yindex=[None,:] (fast for loads, stride-1 in source) and xindex=[:,None] (fast for stores, stride-1 in destination), so both loads and stores are coalesced. This reduced L1TEX stall cycles from ~77 cycles/instruction to ~40, raised L1 hit rate from 0% to 54%, dropped DRAM throughput from 72% to 21%, and improved compute throughput from 19.7% to 43.7%.
slow_pseudocode:
# Non-coalesced: xindex is warp-lane fast dim, but load stride is 128 along x
yindex = yoffset + arange(0, YBLOCK)[:, None]  # slow dim for loads
xindex = xoffset + arange(0, XBLOCK)[None, :]  # fast dim (warp-lane)
y0 = yindex % 128  # stride-1 in input
x2 = xindex        # stride-128 in input -> NON-COALESCED LOAD
load(in_ptr + y0 + 128*x2 + batch_stride*y1)   # stride-128 per lane
store(out_ptr + x2 + out_stride*yindex)         # stride-1 per lane (coalesced)
fast_pseudocode:
# Coalesced: swap arange orientation so each op's fast dim is stride-1
yindex = yoffset + arange(0, YBLOCK)[None, :]  # fast dim for loads (stride-1 in input)
xindex = xoffset + arange(0, XBLOCK)[:, None]  # fast dim for stores (stride-1 in output)
y0 = yindex % 128  # stride-1 in input, now warp-lane fast -> COALESCED LOAD
x2 = xindex        # stride-1 in output, now warp-lane fast -> COALESCED STORE
load(in_ptr + y0 + 128*x2 + batch_stride*y1, mask=xmask & ymask)
store(out_ptr + x2 + out_stride*yindex, mask=xmask & ymask)
# Also add @triton.autotune over XBLOCK/YBLOCK configs
applicable_when: Triton 2D pointwise/transpose kernel where L1/TEX Hit Rate is near 0%, L2 Cache Throughput exceeds 90%, Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction exceeds 50, and the load index has a large stride (>>1) along the warp-lane fast dimension (innermost arange axis) while the store is already coalesced. CPIStall rule triggered with L1TEX stall cycles >30.
do_not_apply_when: Both load and store are already coalesced (L1 hit rate >30%). The tensor layout does not involve a transpose (source and destination strides are both stride-1 along the same axis). Occupancy is the bottleneck rather than memory access pattern. The swap would make stores non-coalesced without a compensating shared memory stage.
framework_notes: Triton-specific: the fast (warp-lane) dimension is controlled by which axis of arange() is [None,:] vs [:,None]. In a 2D tile [XBLOCK, YBLOCK], arange(0,XBLOCK)[:,None] makes X the slow dim and arange(0,YBLOCK)[None,:] makes Y the fast (warp-lane) dim. Swapping these orientations changes which memory dimension is accessed by consecutive threads in a warp. In CUDA, the equivalent is choosing which loop index maps to threadIdx.x.
